    MedEx

    MedEx is an Elixir SDK for recording clinical audio and streaming an independent live WebRTC Opus preview. It accepts indexed mono 48 kHz signed PCM16LE audio, writes an immutable content-addressed WAV artifact, and encodes live Opus for a replaceable WebRTC listener. The host application owns authorization, signaling, and clinical review.

    Installation

    Add :med_ex to your list of dependencies in mix.exs:

    def deps do
  [
    {:med_ex, "~> 0.1.0"}
  ]
end

    Prerequisites

    • Elixir ~> 1.20 (tested on Elixir 1.20.5 / OTP 29.1.2).
    • On Ubuntu 26.04, native WebRTC dependencies (ex_dtls, ex_libsrtp) require a C compiler, make, pkg-config, and OpenSSL development headers (build-essential pkg-config libssl-dev).
    • Live Opus encoding uses membrane_opus_plugin, which downloads precompiled libopus binaries on supported Linux/macOS targets and falls back to system libopus-dev (pkg-config) when building from source.

    Quick example

    # Start a capture under your host DynamicSupervisor (owner is the producer PID)
{:ok, capture} =
  DynamicSupervisor.start_child(
    MyApp.Captures,
    {MedEx.Capture, owner: self(), acquisition_id: "acq-1", artifact_dir: "/var/lib/myapp/wavs"}
  )

# Push contiguous 20 ms chunks (960 mono samples = 1,920 PCM16LE bytes at 48 kHz)
:ok = MedEx.Capture.push(capture, 0, pcm_chunk_0)
:ok = MedEx.Capture.push(capture, 960, pcm_chunk_1)

# Finalize to an immutable "<file_sha256>.wav" file and %MedEx.Evidence{}
{:ok, %MedEx.Evidence{artifact_key: key, file_sha256: sha, sample_count: 1920}} =
  MedEx.Capture.finish(capture)

    Scope in 0.1.0

    • Supported audio profile: Mono 48 kHz signed PCM16LE (up to 30 minutes per capture) with independent send-only WebRTC Opus preview and packaged browser capture/preview JS assets (MedEx.Web.asset_path/1).
    • Out of scope in 0.1.0: Video tracks, multi-channel ECG/PPG waveforms, bundled TURN servers, clinical persistence, and FHIR export.

    Guides

    • Host integration — Elixir capture/preview supervision, Phoenix signaling channel, binary PCM WebSocket contract, and browser hook / AudioWorklet setup.
    • Architecture and roadmap — Capture vs. preview failure domains, shipped vs. planned capabilities, and future integrations.
    • Source development — Working in the source monorepo checkout and preparing Weld release bundles.
